page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is an accelerator-focused virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, configured with 16 shared vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores without multi-threading. Compute resources are coupled with 192 GB of system RAM, offering an allocation of 12 GB per core, alongside a cache topology of 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. Modern vector and machine learning extensions are enabled, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support.

Hardware acceleration is driven by two dedicated NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Single-core processor performance sits within the top decile on stress-ng and Geekbench 6, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,850. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached volumes for persistent data. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 314.07 GB/sec for reads and 145.75 GB/sec for writes, supporting heavy data exchange between host memory and GPU pipelines.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across artificial intelligence and data-intensive tasks. In LLM inference tests, the dual L40S configuration achieves 3,971.95 prompt tokens per second and 389.1 text generation tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models, alongside 37.02 generation tokens per second on 7B models. Throughput slows to 3.91 tokens per second on 70B parameter models, reflecting GPU memory and interconnect boundaries for larger parameter architectures. In-memory data throughput is also robust, demonstrated by Redis benchmark speeds reaching 69.87 million operations per second.

This server type fits mid-tier deep learning inference, distributed machine learning model fine-tuning, computer vision processing, and accelerated scientific computing. The combination of 96 GB total GPU memory and high memory per core offers balanced resource density for modern AI workloads that fit comfortably within the dual-GPU footprint without requiring large-scale distributed clustering.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is an accelerated compute server running on KVM, featuring an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 shared vCPUs at 2.0 GHz and 192 GB of system memory. Designed for parallel processing and artificial intelligence workloads, the instance incorporates two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs with 96 GB of aggregated VRAM. The system features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 BF16 and VNNI, paired with 12 GB of RAM per core. Standard local storage is omitted, requiring external block storage for disk persistence. In performance testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core and multi-core CPU ratings, high uncached memory bandwidth, and strong throughput in lightweight and medium-sized LLM inference tasks. This configuration is engineered for AI model serving, computer vision, data analysis, and parallel computing applications needing dual-GPU acceleration.
